minerals.name: Copper

what_for.text: A strategic mineral for clean energy systems such as wind, geothermal and solar, as well as energy storage, power transmission, electronics and electric vehicles.

source.quote: Copper (Cu) is a strategic mineral for clean energy systems like wind, geothermal and solar technologies
Copper

where_chain_stands.text: Copper is mined and made into a concentrate in Tanzania, then exported. The report found no smelting or refining in the country.

source.quote: At present, Tanzania does not have a smelting or refining factory.

stages.summary: The report does not describe exploration for copper.
The report does not describe mine construction for copper.
Copper is mined at a large scale at the Bulyanhulu gold mine as a by-product of gold. Artisanal and small-scale miners also dig copper ore in several regions, again for export.

source.quote: copper ore is mined on a large scale at the Bulyanhulu gold mine as an associated product of gold extraction

stages.summary: Bulyanhulu ore is made into a copper concentrate in Tanzania, then exported to Japan and China for smelting. The report found no smelting or refining factory in the country.

source.quote: exported to Japan and China for smelting

facts.label: Copper concentrate Bulyanhulu was expected to produce

source.quote: expected to produce 20,000 tons per annum of copper concentrate

facts.note: Expected output, citing Yager (2004). It is not a measured figure.

stages.summary: The copper Tanzania mines leaves as concentrate. The report notes that Tanzania and its neighbours already make significant quantities of copper wire for local construction, vehicles and power transmission, but that Tanzania imports copper cables and foil sheets, and the factories that make cables and transformers here use imported copper.

source.quote: instead imports coppers cables and foil sheets

domestic_vs_export.summary: In 2017 Tanzania banned the export of copper concentrates, but it did not have, and still does not have, installed smelting capacity. The report says exploration activity stood still after the ban.

source.quote: banned the export of copper concentrates to encourage domestic value addition

gaps.text: Tanzania has a fairly strong policy foundation for adding value to minerals, but it lacks a strategic policy to identify, define, categorize and prioritize strategic minerals.

source.quote: it lacks a strategic policy to identify, define, categorize and prioritize strategic minerals

gaps.text: Most existing policies and plans were created before the global focus on the energy transition and do not acknowledge the importance of strategic minerals.

source.quote: Most existing policies and plans were created before

gaps.text: The 2017 export ban on copper concentrates came when Tanzania had no installed smelting capacity.

source.quote: did not (and still does not) have installed smelting capacity

gaps.text: Coordination between the Ministry of Industries and Trade and the Ministry of Minerals is limited.

source.quote: coordination between the Ministry of Industries and Trade and the Ministry of Minerals is limited

options.title: Adopt a cluster model for mineral processing
options.summary: Mining companies form consortiums to build shared processing and smelting facilities, or attract independent investors who focus only on processing. The existing Special Economic Zones and Export Processing Zones already offer incentive packages. The report suggests the Mtwara SEZ, designated the Minerals Corridor, could serve as a graphite processing cluster.

source.quote: Tanzania could adopt a cluster model to develop

options.title: Take a selective approach to downstream value addition
options.summary: Choose carefully which intermediate or final products to make, with the key test being whether they can feed domestic manufacturing. That would allow targeted fiscal incentives. The report’s example: Tanzania and its neighbours already make copper wiring for the local construction, motor vehicle and power transmission markets.

source.quote: Achieving downstream value addition will require

options.title: Consider cross-border cooperation to achieve economies of scale
options.summary: Pursue joint investments and regional trade across the East African Community, COMESA and SADC, and use the African Continental Free Trade Area. Examples in the report: a joint graphite processing facility with Mozambique and Madagascar, and offering to refine ores from the DRC and Zambia at the planned Kahama refinery if there is spare capacity.

source.quote: Tanzania should proactively pursue joint
